task.contract:
**Orchestrator note.** Attempt 2. Your first attempt made real progress (3 files changed, 7 checks run) but ran out of steps before finishing. You now have a governed bootstrap, a checkpoint tool and a larger step budget: continue the work already in your worktree, checkpoint after each step, and finish with an honest verdict.

# WS-F — BC-P2-07: a tier run leaves a third of its declared membership unevaluated and reports it complete  (MEDIUM; blocks AC-5)

## The defect, exactly
`gov health checks` declares 74 checks — all 74 at G5 and 49 at G1. `gov health run --tier G5` evaluates 39 and writes
`complete: true, executed: 39, not_evaluated: 0`; `--tier G1` evaluates 18 of 49 with the same claim. `run_suite` iterates
the governance-suite families only, while `doctor::run` is reached from just two places: the G0 guard's block
re-evaluation and the `gov doctor` CLI. Observable consequence: after a relevant input change `gov health status` reads
GREEN with no failing check while the same output reads `repository.verdict: DEGRADED`, `currency.current: false`, 18 stale
checks; `gov doctor` then makes it YELLOW on D021 — the declared owner of the Gate U `governance_suite_freshness` SLO.
Verifier finding `E-O5-01` (epsilon), residual of iteration-0 `A0-O5-09`.

## What must become true
A tier run evaluates every check its own catalogue declares at that tier, **or** records precisely which members it did not
evaluate and why. Either the tier run executes the doctor half, or the catalogue stops declaring those 35 at G1/G5 and the
record's completeness claim is made true as stated. A completeness claim that is not true is the defect; pick one side and
make the record honest.

## Normative sources (quoted)
- Frozen gate contract AC-5: health-result provenance, and G0-G6 tiers perform their duties.
- Contract v3 O5, and :979-993 for Gate U, whose governance-suite-freshness SLO crosses without reaching the RED/YELLOW/
  GREEN state because its owning check D021 no tier run executes.
- The availability rule: whatever you change must not make a block refuse its own remedy, and must keep refusals typed and
  scoped.

## Acceptance evidence a later verifier will demand
`gov health run --tier G1` and `--tier G5` each evaluate their declared membership, or name every unevaluated member in
`not_evaluated_checks` with a reason; and `gov health status` does not read GREEN while the same output reads
`repository.verdict: DEGRADED` with stale checks.

## Files you own
`runtime/src/scheduler/**` (`run_suite`, tier membership, the health-result summary), `runtime/src/doctor.rs`, and new
tests in `tests/certification/r2_wsf.rs` plus its `mod` line.

## Integration surface
`runtime/src/scheduler/catalogue.rs` is shared with WS-C, which touches only the `D011` and `path_map_compliance` remedy
lists. Stay out of those two lists. Watch the cost of executing more checks per tier run: if a full doctor pass at G1 is
too slow for the G1 contract, that is a real constraint — say so and record the measurement rather than quietly making G1
heavy.

## Mutation scope
Your owned files only.

## Checks available
`build`, `fmt`, `lib_tests`, `cert_wsf`, `cert_ws02` (an existing scheduler/health family that must not regress),
`scheduler_tests`, `doctor_tests`.
